question: I want Veeam Explorer for Microsoft SharePoint to email restored items through an SMTP server with basic auth. What port and server does it use by default, and which port do I need for TLS?
gold_facts: Port 587 should be specified to use TLS encryption.
By default it connects to the smtp.office365.com server.
A 'Connect using SSL' option and an option for SMTP servers requiring authentication (with credentials) are available in the advanced settings.

A.text: By default, Veeam Explorer for Microsoft SharePoint uses port 25 on the mail server to send Microsoft SharePoint items, but you can specify another port in the settings [1][2]. To use TLS data encryption, you need to specify port 587 [1][2]. Note that port 443 is also used and cannot be changed [1][2].

documents.title: Ports
documents.text:
Ports

The following table lists network ports that must be opened for managing traffic during recovery of Microsoft SharePoint data.

For more information on the ports used during backup, see the following sections:

* [Ports](used_ports.html) — for backups created with Veeam Backup \& Replication.
* [Ports](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbo365/guide/vbo_used_ports.html?ver=8) section of the Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 User Guide — for backups created with Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365.

**Ports**

| From | To | Protocol | Port | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Veeam Backup \& Replication console | Backup server | TCP | 443 | Port used to communicate with the backup server. |
| Target SharePoint server | TCP | 80, 443 (according to SharePoint application settings) | Ports used to connect to the target Microsoft SharePoint machine. For more information on recommended port numbers and protocols for SharePoint web application, see [this Microsoft article](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/security-for-sharepoint-server/security-hardening). To discover ports currently used by your SharePoint web application, follow the steps described in [this Microsoft article](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/hh167832(v=nav.70).aspx). |
| Staging server | TCP | 1433 or another port | Ports used to communicate with Microsoft SQL Server machines hosting content databases. Exact port numbers depend on the configuration of Microsoft SQL Server. For more information, see [this Microsoft article](http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/cc646023.aspx#BKMK_ssde). |
| 445 | Port used to connect to Microsoft Domain Services. |
| TCP, UDP, LDAP | 389 | Port used for validating the Microsoft SQL Server machine used as a staging server. |
| Mail server | TCP | 25, 587 or another port, 443 | Ports used for sending Microsoft SharePoint items. Port 25 is used by default, but you can specify another port in the settings. To use TLS data encryption, specify port 587\. Port 443 is also used and cannot be changed. |
| Staging server | Mount server associated with the backup repository | TCP | 3260 to 3270 | Ports used by iSCSI initiator to connect to the iSCSI target. |
| Mount server associated with the backup repository | Backup repository | TCP | 6162 or 2500 to 3300 | Ports used to manage the mounting process. Port 6162 is the default port used to connect to the Veeam Data Mover Service (for Windows\-based backup servers) or Veeam Transport Service (for Linux\-based backup servers). If port 6162 cannot be reached, the first available port in the 2500 to 3300 range is used instead. |

| Note |
| --- |
| To restore database items or lists to a server that is running in a DMZ, the SharePoint web application ports will be used. |

B.text: Veeam Explorer for Microsoft SharePoint establishes a connection to the smtp.office365.com server by default [3]. It uses TCP port 25 by default, and port 587 for TLS [1]. TLS on port 587 enables TLS data encryption [2]. The SMTP server with basic authentication may require credentials including a username such as Administrator [6], and Explorer supports sending SharePoint items as attachments via such a server [7].

sources.paraphrase: Veeam Backup & Replication uses TCP ports 25 (default), 587 (for TLS), or another specified port, and port 443, to send Microsoft SharePoint items via a mail server.

documents.title: SMTP Server with Basic Authentication
documents.text:
[SMTP Server with Basic Authentication › SMTP Server with Basic Authentication]
SMTP Server with Basic Authentication
=====================================

To configure sending Microsoft SharePoint items as attachments using an SMTP server with basic authentication, do the following:


1. In the main menu, click General Options.
2. Open the Mail Settings tab.
3. Select the Enable sending emails check box.
4. From the Mail server drop\-down list, select SMTP server (basic authentication).
5. Click Advanced to configure advanced settings. You can do the following:


* Specify a port number of an SMTP server that you want to use.

The default port number is 25. If you want to use TLS data encryption, specify port 587.

* Select the Connect using SSL check box to establish a secure connection.

* If an SMTP server requires an authentication for outgoing mail, select the The SMTP server requires authentication check box and provide authentication credentials.


![SMTP Server with Basic Authentication](/media/c72e5441-24b5-4db4-a794-132eeaf83ff2/9f01d41ea0d6.png "Configuring Advanced Settings")


> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Advanced SMTP Options' dialog showing settings for an SMTP server with port 587, SSL enabled, and basic authentication configured with a username 'Administrator' and a masked password.


1. In the SMTP server field, specify the address of a server that you want to use as an SMTP server.

By default, Veeam Explorer for Microsoft SharePoint establishes a connection to the smtp.office365\.com server.


1. In the From field, specify the email address to be shown as a sender.
2. In the Send a test email to field, specify the email address to which Veeam Explorer for Microsoft SharePoint sends a test email message.
3. Click Send to send a test email message.
4. Click OK.


![SMTP Server with Basic Authentication](/media/c72e5441-24b5-4db4-a794-132eeaf83ff2/b5a5b4bcb7ab.png "Configuring Mail Settings")


> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Mail Settings' tab in an Options dialog, showing configuration for SMTP server with basic authentication. The SMTP server is set to 'smtp.office365.com', the 'From' field contains 'administrator@tech.local', and a test email is configured to be sent to 'administrator@abc.onmicrosoft.com'.

question: When I create a new virtual lab for SureBackup in Veeam Backup & Replication, what does the description field contain if I leave the default?
gold_facts: The default description contains the user who created the virtual lab.
It also contains the date and time when the lab was created.

A.text: I don't have enough information to answer that from the available sources.

B.text: If you leave the default, the description contains information about the user who created the virtual lab, plus the date and time when the lab was created [1][2].

documents.title: Step 2. Specify Virtual Lab Name and Description
documents.text:
Step 2. Specify Virtual Lab Name and Description
Step 2\. Specify Virtual Lab Name and Description

At the Name step of the wizard, specify a name and description for the virtual lab.

1. In the Name field, enter a name for the virtual lab.
2. In the Description field, provide a description for future reference. The default description contains information about the user who created the virtual lab, date and time when the lab was created.

![Step 2. Specify Virtual Lab Name and Description](/media/df6d74b7-21af-4beb-86d6-1254fb1be2c9/125a0ccd8d6f.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Name' step in the 'New Virtual Lab' wizard, showing fields for entering a virtual lab name ('Vlab22') and description ('Virtual lab for SureBackup job'). The navigation pane on the left highlights the 'Name' step.
